=== THE BUG ===
`exams.questions` is one JSON blob that gets fully overwritten on every save. When the AI generates questions and the instructor then edits them, the original AI draft is gone, so nobody can tell what the instructor actually changed.

=== WHAT TO BUILD ===
When AI-generated questions are first committed into an exam (the moment `exams.questions` is first populated from an AI generation), also store that generated payload into `exams.ai_draft_questions` with `ai_draft_generated_at`. After that, subsequent edits to `questions` must NEVER modify `ai_draft_questions`.

=== ORDER OF WORK (mandatory) ===
This touches existing behavior:
STEP 1 — baseline characterization test that PASSES on unchanged code, pinning that a `questions` update overwrites the stored value wholesale. Capture it passing.
STEP 2 — failing-first test `__tests__/ai-draft-preservation.test.ts` asserting (i) first commit populates `ai_draft_questions`, (ii) a later `questions` update leaves `ai_draft_questions` byte-identical, (iii) a re-generation does NOT overwrite an existing `ai_draft_questions`. Capture it failing for the right reason.
STEP 3 — smallest production change to turn it green.

- `app/api/ai/generate-questions-stream/route.ts` — this is an SSE route using `ReadableStream`; its `finally { controller.close() }` is around lines 324-326. final_response:
Done. Commit `9bdf2b11964c9e78bf6fe77ca693e57ba642a1bb`.

## Key finding that shaped the design

Both AI routes are **pure generators** — `generate-questions/route.ts` and `generate-questions-stream/route.ts` never touch the database. They have no `examId` and no Supabase import; they return questions to the client, which later commits them via `update_exam` / `update_assignment`. So the only place `exams.questions` is ever written is the two handlers.

I also could not add a client-sent `aiGenerated` flag: `updateExamSchema` and `updateAssignmentSchema` are both `.strict()` (an extra key is a hard 400), and `lib/validations.ts` plus the instructor pages are outside the scope list. Provenance therefore had to be inferred server-side, which the spec's own wording licenses — "the moment `exams.questions` is first populated". The rule is: write the draft only when the stored draft is null **and** current questions are empty **and** the incoming array is non-empty.

## STEP 1 — baseline (passing on unchanged code)
```
✓ __tests__/ai-draft-preservation.test.ts (2 tests) 8ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

## STEP 2 — failing first, for the right reason
```
× (i) 문항이 처음 채워질 때 ai_draft_questions 와 생성 시각을 함께 기록한다
AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal [ { id: 'q1', …(2) }, …(1) ]
+ Received: undefined                       ← production never writes the column
× (i) 문항이 처음 채워질 때 초안을 기록한다   (updateAssignment, same reason)
 Tests  2 failed | 7 passed (9)
```
One honest caveat: assertions (ii) and (iii) pass *vacuously* before the fix, since nothing is written at all. They only become load-bearing after (i) starts writing — that is the point of pairing them.

## VERIFY (real output)
1. `npx vitest run __tests__/ai-draft-preservation.test.ts` → `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 9 passed (9)`
2. `npx tsc --noEmit` → `=== tsc exit: 0 ===` (no output)
3. `npm run lint` → `✖ 121 problems (0 errors, 121 warnings)`, exit 0; grep for my three files → `NO LINT OUTPUT FOR CHANGED FILES`
4. `git status --short` → before: clean; after: `M` both handlers + `??` the new test; post-commit: clean

Full suite: **1142 passed / 112 files.**

## MANUAL-QA
(a) first AI commit → `keys: ["questions","updated_at","ai_draft_questions","ai_draft_generated_at"]`, both `true`.
(b) later instructor edit → `keys: ["questions","updated_at"]`, both `false` — absent, not null.
Cleanup: `removed 'ai-draft-payload-qa.mjs'` / `ls: cannot access ...: No such file or directory`.

## Adversarial classes
- **stale_state** — covered by `(iii) 재생성은 이미 저장된 ai_draft_questions 를 덮어쓰지 않는다`. It models the nastiest ordering: instructor deletes every question (so `questions` is empty again, which would otherwise re-trigger "first population") then regenerates. The `ai_draft_questions != null` guard is the load-bearing one; the test compares `JSON.stringify` before/after to prove byte-identity.
- **misleading_success_output** — stating it plainly: **the streaming route has zero test coverage here, and zero production change.** It persists nothing, so there was nothing to await before `controller.close()`; the SSE event protocol and response shape are untouched. Coverage lives entirely at the handler layer because that is the only layer that writes to `exams`. A green suite here is honest only because the streaming route is genuinely not on the write path — not because I mocked it away.
- **dirty_worktree** — clean before, clean after commit (both pasted above).

Not applicable: **malformed input** — handler inputs are already zod-validated upstream and the helper coerces non-arrays via `Array.isArray`; **prompt injection** — no prompt or model output is consumed by this change; **cancel/resume** — no long-running or resumable operation added; **hung commands** — every command finished well under timeout; **flaky tests** — the new tests are pure synchronous payload assertions with no timers or sleeps (the two transient failures in the first full-suite run were pre-existing 5s-timeout flakes in `student-disclosure-ack.test.ts` on a cold 52s transform cache, in files that never call the changed handlers; green on re-run and in isolation); **repeated interruptions** — single uninterrupted session.

## DoneClaim
- **changed_files**: `app/api/supa/handlers/exam-handlers.ts` (new exported `buildAiDraftPreservation`, select widened, conditional assign before update), `app/api/supa/handlers/assignment-handlers.ts` (select widened, conditional assign), `__tests__/ai-draft-preservation.test.ts` (new). Neither AI route was modified — deliberately.
- **tests**: 9 in the new file (2 baseline characterization + 5 `updateExam` + 2 `updateAssignment`); full suite 1142 passing.
- **manual_qa**: both payloads pasted; binary observable satisfied.
- **cleanup**: `/tmp` script deleted, `rm -v` receipt pasted; no DB contact, no `.env*` read, no dependency added.
- **risks**: (1) Provenance is inferred from the empty→populated transition, not from an explicit AI flag — a manually authored *first* question set is also recorded as the "AI draft". Closing this properly needs an `aiGenerated` flag threaded through `lib/validations.ts` and the instructor pages, both out of scope. (2) Both handlers now `select` `ai_draft_questions`, so migration 028 must be applied before deploy or those selects error — note `createExam` has a precedent comment about exactly this hazard for `is_demo`. (3) `updateAssignment` now reads two extra columns per call; negligible, same round trip.
